task: Quality Control Plane semantic execution: make required file deletions first-class actual changes and tombstones in the existing execution route, Plan Before Code and Implementation Sync.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The existing Semantic Execution Intelligence models only files present at the current HEAD. getChangedFiles excludes D status entirely, so a required deletion disappears from the actual verified change set; after deletion the current Atlas also has no node for the file, causing Plan Before Code to report a correctly deleted MUST_EDIT target as outside the generated semantic route. PR #666 reproduced this with src/app/szallitas-es-fizetes/page.tsx.
observableOutcomes: The shared development diff includes deleted paths with explicit deletion status instead of silently dropping them.
buildExecutionRoute can retain deleted planned paths as semantic tombstones in MUST_EDIT while continuing to use the current Atlas for live nodes and consumers.
Plan Before Code accepts a declared required deletion only when the exact deleted path is present in the transaction tombstones and planned envelope.
Edit-Time Implementation Sync counts an actual deletion as satisfying REQUIRED CHANGE SET subset ACTUAL VERIFIED CHANGE SET.
Deleted paths still receive canonical path/domain classification for scope evidence instead of becoming unresolved merely because the HEAD file no longer exists.
unresolvedRisks: Including deletions in every shared development diff can expose latent callers that assumed all changed files still exist.
Treating arbitrary absent planned paths as tombstones would allow a plan to claim a deletion that never occurred.
Rename handling must not double-count the old path as a deletion unless Git reports it as D rather than R.
PO instruction state evaluation must not treat a physically deleted forbidden file as a surviving violation.

in: Existing getChangedFiles transaction diff representation and deletion status parsing.
Existing Atlas execution-route tombstone input and path classification.
Plan Before Code projected/actual scope for deleted paths.
Edit-Time Implementation Sync required-set reconciliation for deletions.
Adversarial regression reproducing the #666 deleted combined-route case.
out: Shipping/payment storefront implementation itself; #666 remains a separate product transaction.
A new gate, tombstone registry, parallel Atlas, or persistent deletion database.
Changing PO instruction meaning or weakening required-change enforcement.
Git history rewriting or automatic branch mutation.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This is a foundational correctness defect in the newly merged two-direction semantic execution model: a required change class (deletion) is invisible to both route generation and actual-diff proof. The highest practical fix is to extend the shared transaction and Atlas route semantics with Git-derived tombstones, preserve path/domain classification, and adversarially prove both false-positive and false-negative boundaries.

acceptanceCriteria: getChangedFiles reports A/C/M/R/D transaction paths and separately identifies D tombstones from git name-status evidence.
A tombstone is accepted into semantic MUST_EDIT only when it both matches the plan pattern and is present in the Git-derived deletedFiles set.
A declared MUST_EDIT path that is absent from HEAD but was not deleted remains outside route and BLOCKs; arbitrary non-existent paths are not legitimized.
A deleted path contributes path-derived domain/authority scope without requiring a live Atlas node.
Edit-Time actualVerifiedChangeSet includes the deleted path, so a required deletion is proven rather than treated as missing.
PR #666's combined-route deletion class is represented without weakening the shipping/payment instruction.
invariants: Current live Atlas nodes remain the authority for live-file semantic consumers and references.
Only Git diff evidence may create a transaction tombstone.
Deletion does not bypass Reference Sync; stale surviving consumers remain blockable.
PO forbidden-state scanning remains fail-closed for surviving files and naturally clears when the forbidden file is actually absent.
Renames continue to be represented as R/current-path changes unless Git explicitly reports a deletion.

failureModes: A D change is omitted by --diff-filter=ACMR and Implementation Sync falsely says the required deletion never happened.
The deleted file is in actual diff but Plan architecture marks it unresolved because only HEAD Atlas nodes are consulted.
buildExecutionRoute accepts every absent exact plan path as a tombstone, allowing invented deletions.
A rename old path is mistakenly treated as a required deletion and pollutes MUST_EDIT.
edgeCases: Deleted static Next.js route that was a PO-forbidden authority.
Deleted non-route source file with a classifiable domain path.
New planned file absent at plan-only time but not a deletion.
R100 rename with old and new path.
Deletion plus stale surviving cross-file consumer caught by Reference Sync.

alternatives.summary: Extend existing transaction diff with D status and pass only Git-proven deleted paths into existing Atlas execution-route reconciliation.
alternatives.reason: It preserves one semantic system and provides provenance that an absent path was actually changed by deletion.

alternatives.summary: Drop deleted files from declared semantic MUST_EDIT after implementation so Plan Before Code can pass.
alternatives.reason: That destroys proof that a required deletion occurred and violates REQUIRED CHANGE SET subset ACTUAL VERIFIED CHANGE SET.

alternatives.summary: Treat any planned path absent from current Atlas as a successful deletion.
alternatives.reason: It cannot distinguish a real deletion from an invented or not-yet-created path and would create a false positive.

specialistReviews.finding: Deletion is a transaction state of an existing code authority, not a new authority type requiring another graph.
specialistReviews.resolution: Carry Git-derived tombstones into the current execution route and use existing path classifiers for scope.

specialistReviews.finding: getChangedFiles is shared by Plan and Edit-Time; fixing only one caller would preserve disagreement between planning and implementation proof.
specialistReviews.resolution: Change the shared diff contract once and consume deletedFiles in both Plan and Edit-Time.

specialistReviews.finding: A naive absent-path fix could legitimize arbitrary missing files and weaken the new bidirectional Implementation Sync.
specialistReviews.resolution: Require exact Git D evidence and regression-test a non-deleted absent path remains BLOCKed.

specialistReviews.finding: Deleted paths still need domain/authority evidence even though their current Atlas node no longer exists.
specialistReviews.resolution: Expose the Atlas's existing path classification as a reusable function and use it only as fallback metadata for tombstones.

challenge.scenario: The required combined route is deleted and disappears from HEAD Atlas.
challenge.resolution: Git D path is supplied as a transaction tombstone and unioned into MUST_EDIT only when it matches the plan envelope.

challenge.scenario: A plan lists a file that never existed or was not changed.
challenge.finding: Absent-from-Atlas alone is insufficient evidence of deletion.
challenge.resolution: No tombstone exists without git name-status D; the declared MUST_EDIT therefore remains outside route and BLOCKs.

challenge.scenario: Edit-Time evaluates a required deleted file.
challenge.finding: Current diff.files omits D, so missingRequired remains true.
challenge.resolution: Shared changed-file contract includes D path in files and deletedFiles; actualChanged therefore proves deletion.

challenge.scenario: Deleted path has no current Atlas node.
challenge.finding: Architecture scope can be falsely unresolved.
challenge.resolution: Use existing canonical-path classifiers as metadata fallback for Git-proven tombstones.

challenge.scenario: A rename is reported by Git.
challenge.finding: Old path could be accidentally considered deletion and satisfy unrelated required removal.
challenge.resolution: Parse name-status explicitly; only status D enters deletedFiles while R contributes the destination to files.

challenge.scenario: Deleting a source contract leaves stale consumers.
challenge.finding: Deletion support must not make stale references invisible.
challenge.resolution: Reference Sync remains independent and runs on the same base/head diff before Implementation Sync decision.

challenge.scenario: PO instruction forbidden state lives in the deleted file.
challenge.finding: Scanning a nonexistent file should not falsely report the state as surviving.
challenge.resolution: Current forbidden-state scanner already returns false when the file does not exist; preserve that behavior.

challenge.scenario: A deletion is outside the planned envelope.
challenge.finding: Including D in actual files could expose an unplanned change that was previously invisible.
challenge.resolution: This is desired: actualSubsetPlanned and Plan Before Code must BLOCK the hidden deletion.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code on the plan-only transaction before implementation.
Unit-test name-status parsing for M, D and R records and prove only D enters deletedFiles.
Adversarially call buildExecutionRoute with a Git-proven tombstone and prove it enters MUST_EDIT; repeat without tombstone evidence and prove it does not.
Regression-test Plan/Edit-Time source contracts include deletedFiles and actualVerifiedChangeSet semantics rather than deleting the declared MUST_EDIT.
Run exact-head full Quality, TypeScript, Production Build, Completion Truth and two-phase CLOSE→LEARN lifecycle before merge.
After merge, rebase/replay #666 unchanged in intent; its deleted combined route must no longer trigger SEMANTIC_MUST_EDIT_OUTSIDE_ROUTE.

requirements.requirement: Git-deleted paths are first-class actual verified changes and only Git D evidence creates deletedFiles tombstones.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: An absent path without Git D evidence must not satisfy a required deletion.

requirements.requirement: The existing semantic execution route and Plan Before Code retain Git-proven planned deletions as MUST_EDIT tombstones with path-derived architecture scope.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A declared required deletion proven by Git D may not be rejected merely because the HEAD Atlas lacks its node.

requirements.requirement: Edit-Time Implementation Sync counts a Git-proven required deletion inside ACTUAL VERIFIED CHANGE SET while preserving stale-consumer and unplanned-change blocking.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Deletion support may not bypass Reference Sync or allow unplanned deletions.

requirements.requirement: The exact implementation head passes TypeScript and production build with the extended shared development-diff contract.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The tombstone semantics repair must not introduce type or production build regressions.

notes: Targeted correction to the existing Semantic Execution Intelligence after #666 proved that required deletions are invisible once the HEAD Atlas node disappears. No parallel gate, no plan weakening, no product implementation in this transaction.
